surfaces.says: git runs an executable named `pre-commit` in the directory `core.hooksPath` names (else `$GIT_DIR/hooks`) before it records a commit, from the top of the working tree, and refuses the commit when it exits non-zero -- taken from githooks(5) and git-config(1) (core.hooksPath, git 2.9+). MEASURED on this machine (git 2.39.1.windows.1): a hook in a core.hooksPath directory ran from the working-tree root with no execute bit (git for Windows runs a file carrying a `#!` line through its bundled sh), and its non-zero exit refused the commit. On a filesystem that keeps modes the hook needs the execute bit, which `activate` sets and `check` reports; UNVERIFIED on such a machine here. The hook hands `git diff --cached --unified=0` itself as the patch; a pure deletion adds no line, so a patch naming no added file is admitted by declaration (`nothing: admitted`). UNVERIFIED: a path git must quote even with core.quotepath off (control characters), and an added line whose own text begins with `++ b/`. `git commit --no-verify` skips every pre-commit hook by git's design: this is the return point for work done in good faith, not a wall against the repository's owner -- a CI projection is the one that cannot be skipped, and is not built.
